finding: src/anomaly/owners.py:122 Canonical-equivalent Unicode identities bypass reviewer independence at both gates.
rationale: The public workflow accepts nonempty identity strings without Unicode normalization, both role-separation checks compare only casefolded text, and the project’s canonical identity function additionally normalizes to NFC, so canonically equivalent composed and decomposed identities can reach and pass both gates.

evidence.output: The task binds the reviewed candidate to gated hash 4a1746f9050120df52e7845166f0ab935c4e584a and records that reviewed product source matches that gate; the supplied review finding is at src/anomaly/owners.py:122.

Gate A/reviewer separation is `reviewer_id.casefold() == gate_a_approver.casefold()` and reviewer/Gate B separation is `journalist_id.casefold() == reviewer_id.casefold()`; `_required_identity` only requires a nonempty string and returns `value.strip()`.
`canonical_key` returns `unicodedata.normalize("NFC", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", value).casefold())`, establishing NFC normalization as part of the project’s canonical identity policy.

`run_workflow` forwards caller gate inputs and dynamic reviewer output into owners; gate mappings restrict field names but not Unicode form, Gate A accepts and persists any nonempty `approved_by`, and review recording only strips `reviewer_id` while its attestation check compares against that same unnormalized value. No upstream NFC guard makes the bypass unreachable.
